    nan = np.isnan(X)
    n = M - nan.sum(axis=1)                       # valid counts

    h = (n + 1) * 0.9 - 1.0
    j = np.floor(h).astype(np.int64)
    j = np.clip(j, 0, np.maximum(n - 1, 0))
    g = h - j
    rows = np.arange(C)
    v1 = Xs[rows, j]
    jj2 = np.minimum(j + 1, np.maximum(n - 1, 0))
    v2 = Xs[rows, jj2]
    use = (g > 0) & (j + 1 < n)

- **Threshold/climatology:** per cell, per day of year, pools of exactly 121 dates (11 baseline anchors 1992–2002 × 11-day calendar windows; Feb 29 values fall into their neighbours' windows); 90th percentile via numpy `quantile(method="hazen")` (Hyndman–Fan type 5), climatology = pool mean; day 60 = mean of days 59/61; then a 31-day centred wrap-around moving mean over the 366-day year — all float64.
